creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 14, item 3.

A `requires` constraint treats an arg with a default as passed. On the left side that fails runs where the user passed nothing; on the right side it lets a default satisfy a requirement the user never met. `excludes` does not do this: it looks at what was actually passed.

```rad
args:
    target str?
    count int = 3
    count requires target
```

```
$ rad requires.rad
Invalid args: 'count' requires 'target', but 'target' was not set
```

And with `password str = "hunter2"` plus `user requires password`, `--user alice` runs. Both reproduce on main. Two scripts broke on the left-side case (`delay d int = 0` with `delay requires capture`; `status int[] = []` with `status requires target`): their plain run exits 1, so both dropped the constraint and check at runtime.

This is deliberate in ra: `flagConfiguredForRelationalConstraints` counts a defaulted flag as set, "so a defaulted flag both triggers its own requires constraints and satisfies others'", pinned by `Test_RequiresWithDefaults_Scenario`. guide/args says the opposite ("when one argument is defined, so must another"), and its sample error text ("was not provided") is not what rad prints.

Decide: evaluate `requires` on the args the user actually passed, as `excludes` does (needs an ra release), or keep the rule and document that a default counts as passing the arg. Fix the guide's sample error text either way.

Where: ra v0.11.0 `ra_cmd_parse.go:2223` (and doc comment at :2532), `ra_test.go:736`; docs at `docs-web/docs/guide/args.md`.
title: requires counts a defaulted arg as passed, on both sides of the constraint
